title: Widow files lawsuit against Regina police
article: A lawsuit filed Friday on the second anniversary of events that led to a Regina man's death blames a lethal combination of pepper spray and physical restraint by police.

Andrea McLean, the widow of Calvin Roy McLean, is suing the City of Regina and Regina Police Service. Her 43-year-old husband died on Oct. 9, 2008, hours after going into medical distress during a struggle with police in the 2200 block of Quebec St.
At the time, police said he was conscious immediately after being handcuffed during his late-night arrest on Oct. 8, 2008, but soon suffered a cardiac arrest. He died in hospital the next afternoon.

Because he died while in police custody, McLean's death is to be the subject of a coroner's inquest. On Friday, a Saskatchewan Justice spokesperson said a date for that hearing has still to be set. An inquest will explore the circumstances of the death, can't assess blame, but can make recommendations for preventing such deaths in the future.
